text:
Maya: Hey team — seeing a weird perf skew in staging around KV cache marshalling + continuous batching. Long-context jobs (40k tokens) slowly grow resident memory over ~10m and then we hit OOMs on a few GPUs. Repro: run `ci/longctx/multi-client` with concurrent batch size 8 + cbatch enabled.
Sam: interesting. any flamegraphs or pprof traces?
Maya: attached a quick pprof snapshot, but here's the hot path: `kvcache::marshal_slot` -> `batch_coordinator::attach_head` -> `kvpager::page_in`. CPU time dominated by `marshal_slot` and we see repeated allocations from slab.
Leo: do we have metrics for head-of-line (HOL) blocking? cbatch can merge batches which pushes a single long ctx ahead and stalls small requests, right?
Maya: yes. Prom shows a growing "kv_slot_hold_seconds" for some slots, correlates with batch merge events. Also high `contbatch_merge_waits_total` spikes.
Arjun: could be fragmentation from repeated partial writes + paging. If marshalling copies frames for each merge we create short-lived allocations that fragment the slab.
Nina: I ran a patch locally that changes marshal to use an arena + reuse buffer and reduced allocs by ~60%. Memory growth stopped in 30m run but HOL latency still high.
Maya: pinging infra-bot to kick off a staging job with the arena patch + new batch split heuristic (split if head ctx > 50% of batch tokens).
infra-bot: Scheduling job: staging-longctx-3945678901-run (pods=6, cbatch=true, batch_size=8, split_threshold_tokens=0.5). Logs will stream to https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/3945
Sam: thanks. Can you paste the small flame snippet?
Maya: sure:
```
(pprof) top
Showing nodes accounting for 38.47s, 92.1% of 41.75s total
      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
    12.30s 29.5% 29.5%     14.10s 33.8%  kvcache::marshal_slot
     9.20s 22.0% 51.5%     11.30s 27.1%  batch_coordinator::attach_head
     3.80s  9.1% 60.6%      9.40s 22.5%  kvpager::page_in
```
Sam: that marshal number looks bad. Any reference to kernel selection or GPU stalls? Might be we push more evictions causing backend kernel thrash.
Leo: kernel selection is orthogonal but relevant: big tails cause different sequence lengths so runtime picks wider kernels and increases per-token mem. If marshal delays before enqueue we compound occupancy.
Arjun: propose short-term: (1) reduce cbatch merge aggressiveness (split large head candidates), (2) reuse marshal buffers per slot, (3) prefetch KV pages async before merge. Long-term: rework slot layout to avoid copy-on-merge.
Nina: implemented (1) + (2) in branch `fix/marshal-tilt`. Ran 2h loadtest: median P95 latency improved 18%, memory plateaued. One regression: slight increase in CPU due to arena bookkeeping.
Maya: can you open an issue and link perf numbers? If infra job passes we'll cut a canary to dedicated. Also add a metric `kvcache_marshal_alloc_bytes` to track.
Nina: filed https://phab.redwood.ai/T12345 with graphs + logs.
Sam: let's be careful about lock ordering — Arena reuse needs to avoid taking slot lock during page IO to prevent deadlocks. Any notes?
Nina: implemented try-lock and fallback path to allocate when lock fails, so we don't block IO threads. Tests look good.
Leo: next steps: run staging canary with kernel selection logging enabled + the arena patch + split threshold 0.5. If stable for 4h, promote. Also schedule a postmortem doc for the fragmentation root causes.
Maya: assigned follow-ups: Nina (marshal patch + metric), Sam (monitoring dashboard + alert), Arjun (eviction tuning + prefetch prototype), Leo (canary + kernel logs).
Arjun: one more datapoint — I saw kvpager evict thrash when quantized models with small KV pages are mixed. We might need model-aware page sizing. Adding to backlog.
Maya: perfect. Thanks all — will update thread after the staging run completes. :thumbsup:
Sam: :rocket:
